problems: Each toast slice's top is made of two separate round lobes, so the slices read as cartoon faces with two eyes, not bread.

Where the crumb discs overlap the crumb box, flat faces sit in the same plane and flicker, leaving dark half-moon marks on the bread. The fix gives each slice one wide domed top: a flattened cylinder for the crust and a matching one for the crumb.

Each toast slice is a box plus an overlapping squashed disc with the same thickness. Their faces sit in the same plane, so a lens-shaped seam shows across the crumb, and the crust has notched 'shoulders' where the box top meets the disc. The slices don't read as single slices of bread. Fix: build each crust and crumb outline from one cylinder, warped into a single bread outline (square bottom, domed crown). Make the crumb slightly thicker than the crust so its face sits just in front.
